spec.full_target: Let n,m be positive integers. Let u:R^n times (0,infinity) -> R^m be jointly smooth, and let q in R^m have Euclidean norm one. Assume: |u(x,r)|=1; for every (x,r), u_tt-Delta_x u=a u for some real a; and on every compact time interval J contained in (0,infinity), u=q outside a compact set C_J uniformly in r. Define e(x,r)=|u_t(x,r)|^2+sum_{j=1}^n|partial_(x_j)u(x,r)|^2 and E(r)=integral over R^n of e(x,r) dx, Lebesgue measure. Prove e(.,r) is Lebesgue integrable for every r>0, E is differentiable at every r>0, and E'(r)=0.
spec.conclusion: For every r>0, e(.,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

hypotheses.statement: For all x∈R^n,r>0 there exists a∈R such that u_tt(x,r)-Δ_xu(x,r)=a u(x,r), with componentwise Δ_x.
For each compact interval J⊂(0,∞), there is compact C_J⊂R^n such that u(x,r)=q for x∉C_J and r∈J.

definitions.definition: E(r)=Lebesgue integral over R^n of e(x,r)

calculations: Finite Euclidean inner-product and finite-sum identities, differentiation of smooth functions and the definition of derivatives. Compactness, uniform continuity, elementary one-variable integration, and iterated integration are established explicitly in the inference arguments; they are not trusted calculation rules.

primitives.meaning: Real field, usual topology, and Lebesgue measure.
k-dimensional real Euclidean space with Euclidean inner product and Lebesgue measure.

propositions.statement: For all x∈R^n,r>0 there exists a∈R such that u_tt(x,r)-Δ_xu(x,r)=a u(x,r), with componentwise Δ_x.
For each compact interval J⊂(0,∞), there is compact C_J⊂R^n such that u(x,r)=q for x∉C_J and r∈J.
For every r>0, e(.,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

locals.type: closed interval contained in (0,∞) with r0 in its interior
locals.declaration: After proving existence of such an interval, choose J about r0.
Choose the compact set furnished by H003 for J.

locals.type: closed box in R^n containing C_J
locals.declaration: After establishing existence of a containing box, choose such a box B.
Fix an arbitrary coordinate index j.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r0>0. Choose δ>0 smaller than r0 and set J=[r0-δ,r0+δ]; this proves F001: such a compact interval exists and r0 is interior. Choose B as below only after its existence is established. H003 applied to J gives a compact C_J with u=q on its spatial complement. Since C_J is compact it is bounded, so some finite closed coordinate box contains it; this proves F002. Choose J using F001, then C_J by H003 and B using F002. For x outside C_J, u is constant in x and in time throughout the interior of J; differentiability gives u_t=0 and every spatial first derivative zero there. On the boundary the same derivatives vanish by continuity, taking a sequence from the open complement. Thus for r∈J all derivatives, and hence e, vanish off C_J. The function e(.,r) is continuous, bounded on compact C_J and zero off it, so is Lebesgue integrable. Also e(x,s) is smooth in (x,s). On B×J its time derivative e_t is continuous and uniformly continuous. For h≠0 sufficiently small with r0+h∈J, the one-variable fundamental theorem of calculus gives [e(x,r0+h)-e(x,r0)]/h=∫_0^1 e_t(x,r0+θh)dθ. Uniform continuity implies uniform convergence in x∈B of this quotient to e_t(x,r0). Since B has finite measure, the absolute difference between integrals is bounded by measure(B) times the uniform error. As E(s)=∫_B e(x,s)dx for s∈J (e vanishes outside C_J⊂B), this proves differentiability and E'(r0)=∫_B e_t(x,r0)dx. Differentiating the finite sum defining e yields e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_j u_j·∂_j u_t, where u_j=∂_j u. For each fixed j, f(x)=u_t(x,r0)·u_j(x,r0) is smooth and compactly supported in C_J; ∂_j f=(∂_j u_t)·u_j+u_t·u_jj. Its integral is zero: choose a coordinate interval containing C_J in its interior; for each fixed choice of the other coordinates, f is zero at both endpoints, and the one-variable fundamental theorem gives integral of ∂_j f equal to zero. The derivative is continuous and compactly supported, hence absolutely integrable; integration first in coordinate j and then in the remaining coordinates is valid by Fubini for an absolutely integrable function. Consequently ∫(∂_j u_t)·u_j=−∫u_t·u_jj. Summing over j gives E'(r0)=2∫_{R^n}u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)dx. Differentiating |u|²=1 in time gives u·u_t=0. By H002, at each x there is a scalar a with u_tt−Δ_xu=a u; thus u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=a(u_t·u)=0 pointwise. The integrand is zero and E'(r0)=0. As r0 was arbitrary, the asserted result holds at every positive time; no endpoint is used.

produces.statement: There exists a compact interval J⊂(0,∞) having r0 in its interior.
There exists a closed bounded coordinate box B⊂R^n containing C_J.
